tags.name: Vault
tags.description: End-to-end-encrypted password vault. The server only stores ciphertext (`v1.<nonce>.<ciphertext>`) and KDF parameters; see the Vault cryptography documentation.

get.description:
KDF parameters and the wrapped vault key. Clients derive the wrap key from the master password locally and unwrap the vault key; a GCM tag failure means a wrong master password.

**Scope:** `vault:read`

post.description:
Stores the KDF parameters and wrapped key generated client-side (VAULT-CRYPTO.md §1). The master password never leaves the client. The server validates the shape only: `kdf` must be `pbkdf2-sha256`, `kdf_iterations` 600 000-10 000 000, `kdf_salt` 16-64 bytes of base64 and `wrapped_key` a sealed 32-byte key.

**Scope:** `vault:write`

put.description:
Replaces KDF parameters and wrapped key. `previous_wrapped_key` must equal the stored value (protects against concurrent changes). Items, `key_id` and `key_check` are untouched because the vault key itself does not change — so this does not lock out anyone who already has an old wrapped key and the old password; `POST /vault/rekey` does. A lower `kdf_iterations` than stored is refused (422) unless `allow_kdf_downgrade` is true.

**Scope:** `vault:write`

409.description: `previous_wrapped_key` does not match the stored key (changed on another device), or the vault is not initialised. `vault_key_changed`: the request names a `key_id` that is no longer the vault's key (the vault was reset and re-created or its key rotated since the client unlocked); drop the key and unlock again.

put.summary: Store the key check of an older vault
put.description:
Stores `key_check` for a vault created before key checks existed. Only a client that has just unwrapped the vault key with the master password should call it. It can be set once: repeating the stored value is a no-op, a different value is a 409. A key rotation replaces it.

**Scope:** `vault:write`

204.description: Stored (or already stored with the same value).

409.description: A different key check is already stored, or the vault is not initialised. `vault_key_changed`: the request names a `key_id` that is no longer the vault's key (the vault was reset and re-created or its key rotated since the client unlocked); drop the key and unlock again.

post.description:
Replaces the vault key and every live record in one transaction (VAULT-CRYPTO.md §2.3). `previous_wrapped_key` and `key_id` must be current and the submitted items and folders must be exactly the live ones at their current revisions; otherwise nothing is changed (409, sync and retry). On success every record's revision is bumped, the vault gets a new `key_id` (writes naming the old one are refused with 409 `vault_key_changed`) and a new sync horizon (every device's next delta sync answers 410). Body limit 64 MiB; larger vaults rotate by export, reset and import.

**Scope:** `vault:write`

409.description: The vault changed meanwhile (`details.reason` = `records_changed`), `previous_wrapped_key` does not match, or the vault is not initialised. `vault_key_changed`: the request names a `key_id` that is no longer the vault's key (the vault was reset and re-created or its key rotated since the client unlocked); drop the key and unlock again.

507.description: `quota_exceeded`: the vault item or size limit is reached.

post.description:
For a forgotten master password: after confirming the **account login password**, irreversibly deletes the key material and every item and folder (tombstones included). Wrong passwords are locked out exponentially per user (5 free failures, then 2^n s up to 15 min) and every attempt is audited (`vault.reset`, `vault.reset_failed`).

**Scope:** `vault:write`

get.description:
Every live folder and item (without `since`), or the folders and items changed after `since` plus the ids of those deleted after it. Pass the previous response's `server_time` as `since`: stamps increase strictly per user, so no change is ever missed. The response is streamed.

A `since` from before the vault was (re-)initialised, older than purged deletion records (tombstones are kept for 180 days), later than the server's clock, or sent while no vault exists (before init, or after a reset) gets **410 `gone`**: sync again without `since` and replace the local copy.

**Scope:** `vault:read`

410.description: `since` is no longer a valid sync position: sync again without it.

post.description:
Stores a new encrypted item under a client-generated id. Limits per user: 50 000 live items and 256 MiB of item data.

**Scope:** `vault:write`

409.description: An item with this id exists (or existed: its tombstone keeps the id taken), or the vault is not initialised. `vault_key_changed`: the request names a `key_id` that is no longer the vault's key (the vault was reset and re-created or its key rotated since the client unlocked); drop the key and unlock again.

422.description: Malformed id or `data`, or `folder_id` names no live folder of yours.

507.description: `quota_exceeded`: the vault item or size limit is reached.

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: The `key_id` of the vault key the client holds (VAULT-CRYPTO.md §2.2); a retired key gives 409 `vault_key_changed`. JSON writes may send it in the body instead (both must agree).

put.description:
Replaces the encrypted data (optimistic concurrency via `base_revision`). Absent `folder_id` keeps the folder; null un-files the item.

**Scope:** `vault:write`

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: The `key_id` of the vault key the client holds (VAULT-CRYPTO.md §2.2); a retired key gives 409 `vault_key_changed`. JSON writes may send it in the body instead (both must agree).

404.description: No such item (or it was deleted).

409.description: `conflict`: the record changed since `base_revision`; `details.current` holds the server copy. `vault_key_changed`: the request names a `key_id` that is no longer the vault's key (the vault was reset and re-created or its key rotated since the client unlocked); drop the key and unlock again.

422.description: Malformed `data`, missing `base_revision`, or `folder_id` names no live folder of yours.

507.description: `quota_exceeded`: the vault size limit is reached.

delete.description:
Deletes the ciphertext; a tombstone is kept (180 days) so other devices learn about the deletion on sync. Deleting an already deleted item answers 404.

**Scope:** `vault:write`

post.description:
Inserts up to 1000 new items in one transaction (used by KeePass/Bitwarden import, which runs client-side). Invalid entries, ids that already exist (also deleted ones), unknown folders and entries beyond the vault limits are skipped and reported in `errors`; the rest are stored. The request body may be up to 32 MiB.

**Scope:** `vault:write`

409.description: The vault is not initialised. `vault_key_changed`: the request names a `key_id` that is no longer the vault's key (the vault was reset and re-created or its key rotated since the client unlocked); drop the key and unlock again.

422.description: `items` is empty or holds more than 1000 entries.

delete.description:
Deletes the folder (a tombstone is kept for sync); its items become unfiled (`folder_id: null`, revision bumped). Sub-folders (names are full paths) are separate folders and are not affected.

**Scope:** `vault:write`

VaultId.description: Client-generated lowercase UUID with hyphens (clients generate version 4; any version is accepted). It is bound into the encryption AAD. Ids are scoped per user, and an id stays taken while its tombstone exists.

VaultSealed.description: Sealed string `v1.<base64 12-byte nonce>.<base64 ciphertext+16-byte tag>` (AES-256-GCM, standard base64 with padding). Opaque to the server, which checks only this shape and the size limits.

VaultKdf.description: KDF parameters and the wrapped vault key, generated client-side at init.

kdf_iterations.description: PBKDF2 iterations (≥ 600 000; clients accept up to 10 000 000).

kdf_salt.description: 16-64 random bytes (clients generate 16), standard base64 with padding.

wrapped_key.description: The random 32-byte vault key sealed with the wrap key derived from the master password (AAD `ludworks/vault/key/v1`): exactly 48 bytes of ciphertext+tag.

key_check.description: Optional (older clients omit it): the key commitment `Seal(vault_key, "", AAD "ludworks/vault/check/v1")`, exactly 16 bytes of ciphertext.

VaultState.description: Key material needed to unlock the vault client-side. Contains no plaintext. Before init `initialized` is false and every other field is null. `key_id` names the current vault key; `key_check` commits to it.

key_id.description: Server-assigned id of the current vault key: new at init and at every key rotation, unchanged by a master-password change. Send it with every write (VAULT-CRYPTO.md §2.2).

key_check.description: `Seal(vault_key, "", AAD "ludworks/vault/check/v1")` (exactly 16 bytes of ciphertext): lets a client holding a remembered vault key check that it is the current one. `null` for vaults created before key checks existed until a client stores one.

VaultKeyChange.description: New KDF parameters and the **same** vault key re-sealed under the new master password. `kdf_iterations` must not be lower than the stored count unless `allow_kdf_downgrade` is set (clients keep max(current, 600000)).

kdf_iterations.description: PBKDF2 iterations (≥ 600 000; clients accept up to 10 000 000).

kdf_salt.description: 16-64 random bytes (clients generate 16), standard base64 with padding.

wrapped_key.description: The random 32-byte vault key sealed with the wrap key derived from the master password (AAD `ludworks/vault/key/v1`): exactly 48 bytes of ciphertext+tag.

previous_wrapped_key.description: The currently stored `wrapped_key` (optimistic concurrency, compared in constant time).

key_id.description: The `key_id` of the vault key this record was sealed under (VAULT-CRYPTO.md §2.2). When it is not the current key the write is refused with 409 `vault_key_changed`. Optional for older clients; current clients always send it.

allow_kdf_downgrade.description: Set only when the user explicitly chose a lower work factor; otherwise a lower `kdf_iterations` than stored is refused with 422.

password.description: The account **login** password (not the master password).

data.description: Encrypted item JSON (AAD `ludworks/vault/item/v1:<id>`), at most 262 144 characters.

revision.description: Incremented by the server on every change (including being un-filed when its folder is deleted).

updated_at.description: Change stamp: strictly increasing per user, so it doubles as the sync position.

folder_id.description: A live folder of yours, or null/absent for no folder.

key_id.description: The `key_id` of the vault key this record was sealed under (VAULT-CRYPTO.md §2.2). When it is not the current key the write is refused with 409 `vault_key_changed`. Optional for older clients; current clients always send it.

folder_id.description: Absent keeps the current folder, null un-files the item, an id moves it to that live folder.

key_id.description: The `key_id` of the vault key this record was sealed under (VAULT-CRYPTO.md §2.2). When it is not the current key the write is refused with 409 `vault_key_changed`. Optional for older clients; current clients always send it.

items.description: Up to 1000 new items (import). Existing ids (also deleted ones) are reported in `errors`, never overwritten. The whole request body is limited to 32 MiB: chunk large imports by size too.

key_id.description: The `key_id` of the vault key this record was sealed under (VAULT-CRYPTO.md §2.2). When it is not the current key the write is refused with 409 `vault_key_changed`. Optional for older clients; current clients always send it.

id.description: The id as sent (at most 64 characters).

error.description: Why the item was skipped, e.g. `an item with this id already exists`, `folder does not exist`, `data must carry ...`, `vault limit reached ...`.

name.description: Encrypted `{"name": "..."}` (AAD `ludworks/vault/folder/v1:<id>`), at most 4096 characters. Names are full `/`-separated paths.

key_id.description: The `key_id` of the vault key this record was sealed under (VAULT-CRYPTO.md §2.2). When it is not the current key the write is refused with 409 `vault_key_changed`. Optional for older clients; current clients always send it.

name.description: Encrypted `{"name": "..."}` (AAD `ludworks/vault/folder/v1:<id>`), at most 4096 characters. Names are full `/`-separated paths.

key_id.description: The `key_id` of the vault key this record was sealed under (VAULT-CRYPTO.md §2.2). When it is not the current key the write is refused with 409 `vault_key_changed`. Optional for older clients; current clients always send it.
The vault key every record in this response is sealed under (`null` without a vault). A client holding a key with another `key_id` must lock instead of using the records.

server_time.description: The user's change clock: the stamp of the newest change included. Pass it as `since` next time; changes committed concurrently with this sync always get a later stamp, so none is missed.

VaultSync.description: Records changed after `since` (all live records without it) and the ids of records deleted after it. A full sync never lists deletions.

VaultConflictError.description: 409 body for a stale `base_revision`: `details.current` is the server copy.

base_revision.description: The item's current `revision` (the version the client re-sealed).

data.description: The item re-sealed under the new vault key (same AAD).

name.description: The folder name re-sealed under the new vault key.

VaultRekey.description: A new vault key: KDF parameters, the new key wrapped under the (new or unchanged) master password, its key check, and every live item and folder re-sealed under it (VAULT-CRYPTO.md §2.3).

kdf_iterations.description: PBKDF2 iterations (≥ 600 000; clients accept up to 10 000 000).

kdf_salt.description: 16-64 random bytes (clients generate 16), standard base64 with padding.

wrapped_key.description: The random 32-byte vault key sealed with the wrap key derived from the master password (AAD `ludworks/vault/key/v1`): exactly 48 bytes of ciphertext+tag.

key_check.description: Key commitment of the NEW vault key (required).

previous_wrapped_key.description: The currently stored `wrapped_key` (optimistic concurrency, compared in constant time).

allow_kdf_downgrade.description: Set only when the user explicitly chose a lower work factor; otherwise a lower `kdf_iterations` than stored is refused with 422.

items.description: Exactly the live items, each at its current revision.

folders.description: Exactly the live folders, each at its current revision.
